title: Seven Winters and One Short Ribbon
subtitle: 节日庆典 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 节日庆典（人与社会·历史、社会与文化）
meta: 主题语境：节日庆典（人与社会·历史、社会与文化）　|　核心词汇：envelope　|　正文 342 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 envelope 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1955 my grandmother ① sealed an envelope that no neighbour in the street would have opened, and she said the sealing was the whole of the winter. The ② envelope, meaning the paper itself and not the letter, ran seven winters and stayed unopened in the book; an envelope, she said, is the only thing in a street that is judged by how long it is left unopened.

Every ③ envelope in that street had the same short ribbon beside it, and the ④ envelope at the far side, meaning the one they kept for the children and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. An envelope, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to open; my grandmother said the opening is the part that fills seven winters.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the envelope was the whole of the parcel, meaning the cover and not the paper. The ⑥ envelope, meaning the cover and not any of that, is the only thing in a parcel that everybody waits for and nobody opens; envelope, he said, is either something you seal or the only word that means both a paper and a cover. He said the cover is the part they remember.

By 1962 the ⑦ envelope had become a line in a list, and the list had become an argument about the short ribbon. The ⑧ envelope of the whole thing, my grandmother wrote in January, was one street and seven winters of opening; envelope, she said, is either the one at the far side or the reason you learned to open. She said the opening was never mentioned.

The ⑨ envelope I remember is the one opened in the list, which closed in 1966 and is still described as the quietest in the street. An ⑩ envelope, my mother said in 1968, is the only one that improves by being opened; every envelope, she said, is a cover that has agreed to look like a paper. She said the cover was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 信封（指街上每一只旁边的那一只）
B. n. 信封（指那一只本身，与信纸相对）
C. 固定搭配：seal an envelope 封上信封
D. n. 信封（指留给孩子的那一只）
E. n. 信封（抽象总称，指一条街上的封缄之事）
F. n. 信封（指礼单上写到、被标名的那一只）
G. n. 封套；外包装（指包裹里人人都等却无人拆开的那样东西）
H. n. 封套（抽象总称，指人人都等却无人拆开的那样东西）

items.q: sealed an envelope that no neighbour in the street would have opened

answers.why: seal an envelope 意为“封上信封”，1955 年祖母封了一只街上没有一位邻居肯拆开的信封。
envelope 意为“信封”，指那一只本身而不是信纸，它经过了七个冬天而在簿子上没有记号。
envelope 意为“信封”，指街上每一只旁边的那一只，每一只旁边都有同一条短短的丝带。
envelope 意为“信封”，指留给孩子的那一只，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
envelope 意为“封套、外包装”，指包裹里人人都等却无人拆开的那样东西，叔叔说这个封套就是那个包裹的全部。
envelope 意为“封套”，指人人都等却无人拆开的那样东西而不是那一只信封，是包裹里人人都等、却无人拆开的东西。
envelope 意为“信封”，指礼单上写到、被标名的那一只，到 1962 年这一只成了礼单里的一行。
envelope 意为“信封”，祖母一月写道，整件事的封缄之事是一条街和七个冬天的拆开。
envelope 意为“信封”，我记得的是礼单上标名的那一只，1966 年结束了，至今仍被说成街上最安静的一只。
envelope 为抽象总称，母亲 1968 年说，一只信封是唯一会因为被好好拆开而变得更好的东西。

叔叔说这个封套就是那个包裹的全部，指的是那个外包装而不是那一只信封。（envelope）
